Subject: Fwd: Dedicated SKU options for Nebula Dynamics — ask from Nebula (24m commit, cold-start preservation)

Ben / Priyom — looping you in. Samir confirmed 24 months and cold-start preservation requirement. He also prefers as-simple-as-possible fleet. Below are workload numbers and my read on priorities.

Workload profile (from Samir + infra):
- Model family: LlamaX-70b (float16 base, will quantize to 4-bit).
- Typical in: 6k tokens; out: 512 tokens. Average response length short but context window huge.
- Steady-state QPS: 8–12. Spikes: 30 qps for bursts (minutes).
- SLA: p95 < 350ms; cold-start max 2s.
- Cost sensitivity: ~target TCO reduction vs hyperscaler endpoints of 35%+ over 24 months.

Preliminary mapping (my lay summary):
- Memory-first (L4-heavy): pair more L4 nodes sized for 32k token working sets. Benefits: fewer cross-node KV loads, cheaper capacitated memory per slot, simpler cold-start behavior for cached prefixes. Drawbacks: L4 currently slower per-GPU perf for generation vs H100; may require slightly higher slot counts to hit p95. Good fit when long-context dominance and cache hit rates are high.
- Throughput-first (H100/A100 mix): H100 for latency-critical frontends (lower per-token latency when batchable), A100 as cheaper throughput layer or for batched background work. Benefits: lower p95 under batching, easier to satisfy p95 for user-facing calls. Drawbacks: memory per GPU lower than L4-equivalent nodes — we must shard KV across GPUs or rely on spill to host which impacts cold-start. Operational complexity increases.

Questions for your teams:
1) Priyom — with their 24m commit, what reserved slot granularity works (slots by GPU or node pool)? Can we propose a 70% reserve on L4 with H100 overflow?
2) Ben — can we draft two price anchors: (A) memory-first: 60% reserved L4 + 40% burst H100; (B) throughput-first: 80% reserved A100 + H100 burst for p95 spikes. Include estimated token cost and 24m blended TCO.

Attached I’ve added the workload CSV and a stub cost workbook: workload-profile.csv, cost-estimate-2yr.xlsx.

If we converge quickly I’ll send Samir a short SOW addendum with an ops runbook and canary plan.

Thanks,
Soojin

Team / Samir — quick recommendation based on Priyom’s aside on tiling and our cost model:

Recommendation (short):
- Offer Path A (Memory-first) as primary: 60% L4 nodes reserved sized for 32k working sets + 40% H100 burst pool. Rationale: guarantees cold-start behavior, simplifies KV locality, achieves 35–40% TCO reduction vs hyperscaler given their 24-month commit and high cache hit expectations.
- Provide Path B (Throughput-first) as optional alternate: 80% A100 reserved (dense throughput) + 20% H100 for latency spikes. Rationale: lower per-token latency under batch but higher operational complexity and risk of cold-start stalls for very long contexts.

Operational mitigations to include in SOW:
- Prefix caching policy: aggressive hot-prefix pinning for top 5% of flows to reduce cross-node fetches.
- Canary rollout: 2-week canary (10% of traffic) on Path A before full cutover; measure cold-start p95 and cache hit.
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to H100 pool if any instance exceeds 1.5x expected tail latency.

Pricing ask: we should present a blended per-token and per-reserved-slot price. I’ll draft anchors tonight; Ben — will add an appendix on expected slot-utilization and buffer headroom.

Samir — if you’re comfortable with architecture, we’ll attach the canary runbook and draft SOW for signature. Otherwise tell us which path you prefer and we’ll iterate.

Thanks,
